item.title: Stories on Stage: Catriona McPherson & Karen Levy — Sun Sep 13, 2:00 PM — Sudwerk Brewing Co.
item.description:
Short fiction read by actors. Catriona McPherson is a Scottish writer. She is most notable for her Dandy Gilver series. Her novels have won an Agatha Award, two Anthony Awards, six Lefty Awards, and two Macavity Awards. Karin Levy is an Israeli-American writer and author of memoir My Father’s Gardens.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Sun Sep 13, 2:00 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz — Tue Sep 15, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz Tuesdays, 10 AM – 12 PM | September 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 $170 Members, $190 Non-Members (Materials not included) This 5-week workshop with Misuk Goltz will focus on using your brushes to their full potential and practicing diverse hand motions to achieve painterly, expressive watercolor paintings. Students will learn how to distribute different values to create balanced and sophisticated artwork while painting various subjects. Please note that this class is intended for participants who have previous experience with watercolor techniques and color blending. The use of high-quality watercolor materials is strongly recommended to achieve the best results. Register here: https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: "Google: The Genealogist's Best Friend” by Dr. James Baker — Tue Sep 15, 1:00 PM — Davis Senior Center
item.description: The Davis Genealogy Club presents, “Google: The Genealogist’s Best Friend” by Dr. James Baker, on Tuesday, September 15th, at 1 PM at the Davis Senior Center, 646 A Street, Davis. The public is invited to this free virtual program designed for curious researchers at all levels and shown on the big screen. Does Google “know” anything about genealogy? Well yes–perhaps more you realize. In this talk, Dr. Baker will explain how using Google’s different applications including images, books, maps, and its advanced search capabilities, can help us with our genealogy research. James Baker has been an active genealogist for the past 17 years. He specializes in German, Midwest US, early American research, and DNA. View the presentation alongside club members and enjoy refreshments, or participate via Zoom by emailing President@DavisGenealogy.org to request a guest pass. Baker is one of the club’s favorite presenters. Mark your calendar for this fun and helpful demonstration, and stop by early to

item.title: University Farm Circle Newcomers Welcome — Wed Sep 16, 9:30 AM — Unitarian Universalist Church of Davis
item.description:
University Farm Circle ( UFC) is a philanthropic, educational and social programs organization. UFC invites all Yolo County and surrounding area residents to our annual Newcomers Welcome on Wednesday, September 16th, from 9:30 to 11:30 AM at the Unitarian Universalist Church 27074 Patwin Road, Davis CA. At the UFC Newcomers Welcome you’ll meet like-minded people looking to foster new friendships, experiences and hear more about what UFC has to offer. There will be a short presentation by Board Members to familiarize you with all UFC has to offer an answer any questions you may have. You will also explore and sign up for our diverse array of special interest groups. UFC offers more than 60 groups – everything from wine tasting, book groups, mahjong, pickleball, paddle boarding, foreign language and lunch groups. Light refreshments will be provided. For more information and registration by September 15th, check the online calendar www.ufcdavis.org.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:
Backyard Book Swap with Yolo County Caregivers Collective 2nd Sunday of every month, 10am – 12pm 1118 L Street, Davis
Ready for a new read? Join our monthly book swap! This free playgroup meets on the second Sunday of every month. Bring a gently-loved book or two to swap, discover your mini’s next favorite read, and connect with other bookworms. Our book swap is a great way to refresh your bookshelf, make new friends, and add an exciting new chapter to your social life! We’ll have bubbles, simple arts, and space to play for the little ones. Each month features a different theme and free refreshments will be provided too. Together we can build community around the joy of reading.
Source: The Dirt

Tour resident artist studios, explore our contemporary gallery, and learn about the artistic processes of our local creators. Is there a fee? This event is free and open to the public. What is the Atelier? Located in Midtown Sacramento, The Atelier is a contemporary studio and gallery dedicated to empowering creators of all ages.

item.title: Second Sunday Bingo — Sun Sep 13, 12:00 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
Odd Fellows Bingo (LH)
When: Second Sunday of the month Where: 415 2nd St, Davis, CA 95616, USA (map)
Description: Second Sunday Bingo at the Lodge. Doors open at noon and Bingo begins at 1 p.m. Open to all adults. Davis Odd Fellows Bingo! is a wonderful way for the community to support the many needy non-profit organizations here in Davis. Each month, Davis Odd Fellows Bingo! connects with a local organization that needs assistance. Community members, friends, and family are encouraged and welcomed to come to the Davis Odd Fellows Lodge for an afternoon of to fun playing Davis Bingo. For as little as $12, you can sit with friends and chat or meet new people while helping people in our community.

item.title: Talk Theology to Me: Questions about Faith & Life — Tue Sep 29, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community What questions about faith, God, Scripture, or spirituality have you been carrying around?
**Talk Theology to Me** is an informal, discussion-based gathering for anyone who is curious about faith and the questions that shape our lives. No theological degree—or even a fully formed belief system—is required. Just bring your questions and your willingness to listen and explore. Together, we’ll have a facilitated conversation drawing from **Scripture, theology, and lived experience**. We’ll make room for curiosity, uncertainty, different perspectives, and the kinds of questions that don’t always have easy answers.
### What to expect
* A welcoming, low-pressure conversation * Space to ask honest questions about faith and spirituality * Reflection on Scripture and our own lived experiences * Respect for different perspectives and places in the faith journey * An opportunity to connect with others in a meaningful way
This is a space for exploration rather than deba

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Sep 30, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: National Disability Employment Awareness Month 2026 — Thu Oct 1
item.description:
Since the 1970s, National Disability Employment Awareness Month (NDEAM) has taken place every October. NDEAM reinforces the message across the U.S. that people with disabilities provide invaluable roles and perspectives to our diverse American workforce. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that one in four adults (at least 60 million) in the U.S. live with a disability. This statistic is based on what is reported, however. So, it’s possible that the number is higher than what is stated.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Voting from Different Perspectives: Studying Elections across Disciplines — Tue Oct 27, 3:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Presented by Inclusive Excellence (Campus Community Book Project) This panel brings together faculty from across UC Davis and UC Davis Health discuss their research on voting and elections within and between different disciplines as well as national and international contexts. The panel aims to share research, advance research literacy, and explore scholarly boundaries of expertise as well as areas for cross-pollination. Panelists will include:
Vikram D. Amar, Daniel J. Dykstra Distinguished Professor of Law Ruth Shim, Director of Cultural Psychiatry and Luke & Grace Kim Professor in Cultural Psychiatry, Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences Lauren Young, Associate Professor and Director of Graduate Studies, Political Science Megan Macklin (moderator), Director of Campus Climate and Inclusion Initiatives, Office of Campus and Community Relations/Inclusive Excellence
You must register in advance for this event.
